findings.title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
findings.body: If `embed_category` is blank or has no matching category, this query returns no rows and indexing `[0]['id']` raises before the fallback below can run. Since the old setting defaults to blank, upgrades without an explicitly configured embed category can fail during migration, blocking the upgrade.

findings.title: Legacy hosts with schemes are migrated in a form that never matches
findings.body: This inserts the old setting value verbatim, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. Existing configurations may contain entries such as `http://example.com` (which the old host check accepts), but `record_for_host` later looks up only the parsed hostname `example.com`; those migrated entries will no longer authorize embeds.

findings.title: Configured ports are discarded during host lookup
findings.body: The model accepts and retains entries such as `example.com:8080`, but `URI(host).host` returns only `example.com`, without the port. This query therefore cannot find a configured host with a port, so embeds from that origin are rejected despite the entry passing validation.

findings.title: Valid domains with longer top-level domains are rejected
findings.body: The format limits the final label to 2–5 letters, so valid domains such as `example.museum` cannot be saved. Administrators cannot allow embeds from domains using longer top-level domains.

findings.title: A null host raises before validation can report an error
findings.body: When a create or update request supplies `host: null`, `self.host` is nil and calling `sub!` raises `NoMethodError` in the validation callback. The request returns a server error instead of the normal validation response for a missing host.

findings.title: Duplicate host records make category routing ambiguous
findings.body: The model and table do not enforce host uniqueness, while this lookup returns only one matching record. Administrators can create the same hostname with different categories; imported topics then use only the first matching record's category, so the other association is silently ignored.
